draft.title: Food chains and food webs
card: Food chain
A food chain shows one feeding path, such as grass, then a grasshopper, then a lizard.
Arrows
Each arrow points from the food to the eater. The arrow means "is eaten by", so it points toward the organism doing the eating.
Food web
Most organisms eat more than one thing and are eaten by more than one thing. A food web joins many food chains together to show these links.
Dependence
A food web shows how the organisms in an ecosystem depend on each other for food.
draft.remember: A chain is one path with arrows from food to eater. A web joins many chains.

a.q: In a food chain, a frog eats a fly. Which arrow is drawn correctly?
opts: Fly → frog
Frog → fly
Fly ← frog, pointing at the fly
Frog and fly joined by a line with no arrowhead
a.why: The arrow points from the food to the eater, so it goes from the fly to the frog. Frog → fly is tempting because it looks like the frog is acting on the fly, but that shows the wrong direction of feeding.
a.clue: Point the arrow toward the eater.

b.q: On a Tasmanian farm, a food chain shows grass → rabbit → eagle. Another shows grass → mouse → eagle. Why is it better to show both chains in one food web?
opts: It shows grass and eagle each link to more than one organism
It shows that rabbits and mice eat each other
It shows the eagle makes its own food from grass
It shows the arrows should point from eater to food
b.why: A food web joins chains, so it shows that grass feeds both animals and the eagle eats both. The idea that rabbits and mice eat each other is wrong, because neither chain has an arrow between them.
b.clue: Look for what the two chains share.

b.best: It shows grass and eagle each link to more than one organism

problems.detail: "Most organisms eat more than one thing" is loose. Producers such as grass do not eat anything, so "most animals" or "most consumers" would be accurate.

check.summary: Both questions have one clearly right answer, and the explanations match the card. The only issue is a minor wording slip: the card says "most organisms eat more than one thing", although producers do not eat.

proposal.title: Food chains and food webs
card: Food chain
A food chain shows one feeding path, such as grass, then a grasshopper, then a lizard.
Arrows
Each arrow points from the food to the eater. The arrow means "is eaten by", so it points toward the organism doing the eating.
Food web
Most animals eat more than one kind of food, and many are eaten by more than one kind of animal. A food web joins many food chains together to show these links.
Dependence
A food web shows how the organisms in an ecosystem depend on each other for food.
proposal.remember: A chain is one path with arrows from food to eater. A web joins many chains.

a.q: In a food chain, a frog eats a fly. Which way should the arrow point?
opts: From the fly to the frog
From the frog to the fly
Both ways between the fly and frog
No arrow, just a line between them
a.why: The arrow points from the food to the eater, so it goes from the fly to the frog. From the frog to the fly is tempting because the frog seems to act on the fly, but that shows the wrong direction of feeding.
a.clue: Point the arrow toward the eater.

b.q: On a Tasmanian farm, a food chain shows grass → rabbit → eagle. Another shows grass → mouse → eagle. Why is it better to show both chains in one food web?
opts: It shows grass and the eagle each link to two animals
It shows that rabbits and mice feed on each other
It shows that the eagle feeds directly on the grass
It shows arrows point from the eater to the food
b.why: A food web joins chains, so it shows that grass feeds both the rabbit and the mouse, and the eagle eats both. The idea that rabbits and mice feed on each other is wrong, because neither chain has an arrow between them.
b.clue: Look for what the two chains share.

a.best: From the fly to the frog

b.best: It shows grass and the eagle each link to two animals
